source.text: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις Ἁνανίας ὀνόματι σὺν Σαπφίρῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπώλησεν κτῆμα καὶ ἐνοσφίσατο ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς, συνειδυίης καὶ τῆς γυναικός, καὶ ἐνέγκας μέρος τι παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔθηκεν.

records.literal_gloss: A man now certain Ananias by name with Sapphira the wife of him sold a property, \v 2 and he kept back from the price, being aware also the wife, and having brought a part certain at the feet of the apostles he laid [it].

en.L: Now a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a property, \v 2 and he kept back [some] of the price, his wife also knowing [of it], and bringing a certain part, he laid [it] at the feet of the apostles.
en.B: A man called Ananias, however, sold a piece of land together with his wife Sapphira. \v 2 He secretly set aside some of the proceeds, and his wife knew of it. Then he brought the remaining portion and laid it at the apostles' feet.
en.R: But there was a man named Ananias. He and his wife Sapphira sold some land. \v 2 Ananias kept part of the money for himself, and his wife knew about it. He brought the rest of the money and gave it to the apostles, as if it were all of it.

es.L: Pero cierto hombre llamado Ananías, con Safira su esposa, vendió una propiedad, \v 2 y apartó para sí [parte] del precio, sabiéndolo también la esposa, y trayendo cierta parte, [la] puso a los pies de los apóstoles.
es.B: Sin embargo, un hombre llamado Ananías vendió un terreno junto con su esposa Safira. \v 2 A escondidas se quedó con parte del dinero, y su esposa lo sabía. Luego llevó el resto y lo puso a los pies de los apóstoles.
es.R: Pero había un hombre llamado Ananías. Él y su esposa Safira vendieron un terreno. \v 2 Ananías se quedó con una parte del dinero, y su esposa lo sabía. Llevó el resto del dinero y se lo dio a los apóstoles, como si fuera todo.

fr.L: Or un homme nommé Ananias, avec Saphira sa femme, vendit une propriété, \v 2 et il détourna [une partie] du prix, sa femme le sachant aussi, et apportant une certaine part, il [la] déposa aux pieds des apôtres.
fr.B: Un homme du nom d’Ananias, cependant, vendit un terrain avec sa femme Saphira. \v 2 Il mit secrètement de côté une partie de l’argent, et sa femme le savait. Puis il apporta le reste et le déposa aux pieds des apôtres.
fr.R: Mais il y avait un homme qui s’appelait Ananias. Lui et sa femme Saphira ont vendu un terrain. \v 2 Ananias a gardé une partie de l’argent pour lui, et sa femme le savait. Il a apporté le reste de l’argent et il l’a donné aux apôtres, comme si c’était tout.

sw.L: Lakini mtu mmoja jina lake Anania, pamoja na Safira mkewe, aliuza kiwanja, \v 2 akajiwekea [sehemu] ya thamani yake, mkewe naye akijua, na akileta sehemu fulani, akaiweka miguuni pa mitume.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, mtu mmoja aitwaye Anania aliuza kiwanja pamoja na mkewe Safira. \v 2 Akajiwekea kwa siri sehemu ya fedha walizopata, na mkewe alijua jambo hilo. Kisha akaleta sehemu iliyobaki, akaiweka miguuni pa mitume.
sw.R: Lakini palikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Anania. Yeye na mkewe Safira waliuza kiwanja. \v 2 Anania alijiwekea sehemu ya fedha, na mkewe alijua habari hiyo. Akaleta fedha zilizobaki akawapa mitume, kana kwamba ndizo fedha zote.

decisions.choice: now, but: a contrast with Barnabas just before
alternatives: a new story with no link
decisions.reason: 4:36-37 tells how Barnabas sold a field and laid all the money at the apostles' feet. Ananias does the same outwardly, but not honestly.

decisions.choice: kept back: the word used of Achan, who kept back what belonged to God
decisions.reason: The verb means to set aside for oneself, to pilfer (Titus 2:10). The Greek Old Testament uses it in Joshua 7:1, where Achan secretly took for himself what had been given over to God, at the start of Israel's life in the land. Here too sin threatens a new people of God at its start.

decisions.choice: his wife also knowing: she shared in the plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to know together with someone, to be in on it. 5:9 says they agreed together.

decisions.choice: laid it at the feet of the apostles: handed it over to the apostles' care
decisions.reason: The same act as in 4:35 and 4:37. The apostles gave out the money to anyone in need (4:35).

decisions.choice: as if it were all of it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deception was. Peter's questions (5:3-4, 5:8) show that Ananias presented the part as the whole price.

decisions.choice: apartó para sí (L); se quedó con (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to set aside for oneself part of what was handed over, the word used of Achan (meaning decision m2). "Apartar para sí" keeps that at Literal; Balanced and Readable say plainly that he kept it. Peter repeats the verb in 5:3, and Spanish repeats the same words there.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), with the imperfect for background
decisions.reason: As in the Gospels and in Acts 4 (style guide §3, §9): the passé simple is the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé. Speech keeps the tenses of speech. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: kujiwekea
decisions.reason: The verb means to set aside for oneself part of what was handed over, the word used of Achan (meaning decision m2). "Kujiwekea" (to keep back for oneself) says that without the sense of hiding ("kuficha") or plain theft ("kuiba"). Peter repeats the verb in 5:3, and Swahili repeats the same word there.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἁνανία, διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου, ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου;

records.literal_gloss: Said but the Peter, Ananias, why filled the Satan the heart of you, to lie you the Spirit the Holy and to keep back from the price of the land?

en.L: But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, [for] you to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back [some] of the price of the land?
en.B: Peter said, "Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart, to make you lie to the Holy Spirit and keep part of the land's price back?
en.R: Peter said, "Ananias, why did you let Satan take control of your heart? You lied to the Holy Spirit. You kept some of the money from the land for yourself.

es.L: Pero Pedro dijo: «Ananías, ¿por qué llenó Satanás tu corazón, para que mintieras al Espíritu Santo y apartaras para ti [parte] del precio del terreno?
es.B: Pedro le dijo: «Ananías, ¿por qué llenó Satanás tu corazón, hasta hacerte mentir al Espíritu Santo y quedarte con parte del precio del terreno?
es.R: Pedro le dijo: «Ananías, ¿por qué dejaste que Satanás se adueñara de tu corazón? Le mentiste al Espíritu Santo. Te quedaste con una parte del dinero del terreno.

fr.L: Mais Pierre dit : « Ananias, pourquoi Satan a-t-il rempli ton cœur, [pour que] tu mentes à l’Esprit Saint et que tu détournes [une partie] du prix du terrain ?
fr.B: Pierre lui dit : « Ananias, pourquoi Satan a-t-il rempli ton cœur, au point de te faire mentir à l’Esprit Saint et garder pour toi une partie du prix du terrain ?
fr.R: Pierre lui a dit : « Ananias, pourquoi as-tu laissé Satan prendre le contrôle de ton cœur ? Tu as menti à l’Esprit Saint. Tu as gardé pour toi une partie de l’argent du terrain.

sw.L: Lakini Petro alisema, "Anania, kwa nini Shetani ameujaza moyo wako, [hata] umwongopee Roho Mtakatifu na kujiwekea [sehemu] ya thamani ya kiwanja?
sw.B: Petro alisema, "Anania, kwa nini Shetani ameujaza moyo wako hata ukamwongopea Roho Mtakatifu, ukajiwekea sehemu ya thamani ya kiwanja?
sw.R: Petro alisema, "Anania, kwa nini ulimwacha Shetani autawale moyo wako? Umemwongopea Roho Mtakatifu. Umejiwekea sehemu ya fedha za kiwanja.

decisions.choice: Satan filled your heart: Satan took hold of his thinking and will
decisions.reason: Luke says Satan entered Judas (Luke 22:3). The believers have just been filled with the Holy Spirit (4:31); Ananias let another power fill him. Peter still holds him to account (5:4).

decisions.choice: to lie to the Holy Spirit: to lie to God
alternatives: to lie only to the apostles
decisions.reason: Peter says in 5:4 that Ananias lied to God. The Spirit was present in the community and its leaders, so lying to them was lying to the Spirit, and to God.

decisions.choice: keep back: the same verb as in 5:2
decisions.reason: He kept for himself part of what he claimed to have given.

decisions.choice: to lie: the result of Satan's filling
decisions.reason: The infinitive says what came of it: he lied and kept money back.

decisions.choice: why did you let Satan take control of your heart?
alternatives: why has Satan filled your heart?
decisions.reason: Readable puts Ananias's own part in the question, as 5:4 does ("why did you put this in your heart?").

source.text: οὐχὶ μένον σοὶ ἔμενεν καὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχεν;

records.literal_gloss: Not remaining to you was it remaining, and having been sold in the your authority was it?

en.L: While it remained, did it not remain yours? And when it was sold, was it not in your authority?
en.B: Before it was sold, was it not your own? And after the sale, was the money not yours to use as you chose?
en.R: The land belonged to you before you sold it. And after you sold it, you could do what you wanted with the money.

es.L: Mientras quedaba [sin vender], ¿no seguía siendo tuyo? Y una vez vendido, ¿no estaba bajo tu autoridad?
es.B: Antes de venderlo, ¿no era tuyo? Y después de la venta, ¿no era tuyo el dinero para usarlo como quisieras?
es.R: El terreno era tuyo antes de venderlo. Y después de venderlo, podías hacer lo que quisieras con el dinero.

fr.L: Tant qu’il restait, ne restait-il pas à toi ? Et une fois vendu, n’était-il pas en ton pouvoir ?
fr.B: Avant d’être vendu, ne t’appartenait-il pas ? Et après la vente, l’argent n’était-il pas à ta disposition ?
fr.R: Le terrain était à toi avant que tu le vendes. Et après l’avoir vendu, tu pouvais faire ce que tu voulais de l’argent.

sw.L: Je, kilipobaki [bila kuuzwa], hakikubaki kuwa chako? Na kilipokwisha kuuzwa, je, hakikuwa katika mamlaka yako?
sw.B: Kabla hakijauzwa, je, hakikuwa chako? Na baada ya kukiuza, je, fedha hazikuwa zako kuzitumia upendavyo?
sw.R: Kiwanja kilikuwa chako kabla hujakiuza. Na baada ya kukiuza, ungeweza kuzitumia fedha kama ulivyotaka.

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: Peter is not asking for information. He is saying that the land and the money were Ananias's own.

decisions.choice: giving was free: the sin was the lie, not keeping the money
alternatives: everyone had to sell all they had
decisions.reason: The believers shared willingly (4:32-35). Ananias could have kept the land or the money. What he did wrong was to pretend.

decisions.choice: in your authority: under your control, yours to decide
decisions.reason: The word means power or right to act.

decisions.choice: two plain statements
decisions.reason: Readable states what Peter's questions imply.

decisions.choice: mamlaka
decisions.reason: The word means that the money was under his control, his to decide (meaning decision m3). "Mamlaka" is the word for this Greek term across the New Testament drafts; "haki" is kept for righteousness.

source.text: τί ὅτι ἔθου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο;

records.literal_gloss: Why [is it] that you put in the heart of you the deed this?

en.L: Why is it that you have put this deed in your heart?
en.B: Why did you set your heart on doing this?
en.R: Why did you decide to do this?

es.L: ¿Por qué [es] que pusiste en tu corazón esta acción?
es.B: ¿Por qué decidiste en tu corazón hacer esto?
es.R: ¿Por qué decidiste hacer esto?

fr.L: Pourquoi as-tu mis dans ton cœur cette action ?
fr.B: Pourquoi as-tu décidé dans ton cœur d’agir ainsi ?
fr.R: Pourquoi as-tu décidé de faire cela ?

sw.L: Kwa nini umeliweka jambo hili moyoni mwako?
sw.B: Kwa nini uliamua moyoni mwako kufanya jambo hili?
sw.R: Kwa nini uliamua kufanya hivi?

decisions.choice: put in your heart: decide, make up one's mind
decisions.reason: Luke 21:14 uses the same idiom: "settle it in your hearts".

decisions.choice: Satan filled his heart, yet he chose it
decisions.reason: Peter asked why Satan filled his heart (5:3); now he asks why Ananias himself planned it. Both are true.

source.text: οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Not you lied to men but to the God.

en.L: You did not lie to {{gender:people|men}} but to God."
en.B: It is not human beings you have lied to, but God."
en.R: You did not lie to people. You lied to God!"

es.L: No mentiste a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, sino a Dios».
es.B: No es a seres humanos a quienes has mentido, sino a Dios».
es.R: No les mentiste a las personas. ¡Le mentiste a Dios!».

fr.L: Tu n’as pas menti à {{gender:des humains|des hommes}}, mais à Dieu. »
fr.B: Ce n’est pas à des êtres humains que tu as menti, mais à Dieu. »
fr.R: Tu n’as pas menti aux gens. C’est à Dieu que tu as menti ! »

sw.L: Hukuwaongopea watu, bali Mungu."
sw.B: Hukuwaongopea wanadamu, bali umemwongopea Mungu."
sw.R: Hukuwaongopea watu. Umemwongopea Mungu!"

decisions.choice: not to people but to God: above all to God
alternatives: he had not lied to the apostles at all
decisions.reason: He did deceive the apostles. The "not ... but" form puts all the weight on the second part, as in Exodus 16:8, where Moses tells Israel their grumbling is "not against us but against the Lord".

decisions.choice: lying to the Holy Spirit (5:3) is lying to God
decisions.reason: Peter uses the two sayings of the same lie. The Spirit is God present with his people.

decisions.choice: people: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, as against God.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as the meaning note explains; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek means human beings (meaning decision m3), and Spanish has both wordings, so the reader setting chooses.

source.text: ἀκούων δὲ ὁ Ἁνανίας τοὺς λόγους τούτους πεσὼν ἐξέψυξεν· καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας.

records.literal_gloss: Hearing now the Ananias the words these, having fallen he breathed out; and came fear great upon all those hearing.

en.L: And Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last; and great fear came upon all who heard [of it].
en.B: As Ananias heard these words he fell down and died, and a great fear came over everyone who heard about it.
en.R: When Ananias heard this, he fell down dead. Everyone who heard about it was very afraid.

es.L: Y al oír Ananías estas palabras, cayó y expiró; y vino un gran temor sobre todos los que [lo] oían.
es.B: Al oír Ananías estas palabras, cayó al suelo y murió, y un gran temor se apoderó de todos los que se enteraron.
es.R: Cuando Ananías oyó esto, cayó muerto. Todos los que se enteraron de lo sucedido sintieron mucho miedo.

fr.L: Et Ananias, entendant ces paroles, tomba et expira ; et une grande crainte s’empara de tous ceux qui [l’]apprenaient.
fr.B: En entendant ces paroles, Ananias tomba et mourut, et une grande crainte saisit tous ceux qui l’apprirent.
fr.R: Quand Ananias a entendu cela, il est tombé mort. Tous ceux qui l’ont appris ont eu très peur.

sw.L: Na Anania aliposikia maneno haya, alianguka, akakata roho; na hofu kuu ikawajia wote waliosikia.
sw.B: Anania aliposikia maneno hayo alianguka, akafa, na hofu kubwa ikawaingia wote waliosikia habari hiyo.
sw.R: Anania aliposikia hayo, alianguka akafa. Kila mtu aliyesikia habari hiyo aliogopa sana.

decisions.choice: breathed his last: died
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe out one's life. Luke uses it again of Sapphira (5:10) and of Herod (12:23), each struck down by God.

decisions.choice: his death was God's judgment
decisions.reason: Peter pronounces no sentence on Ananias. His death follows at once on his lie to God (5:4), and the fear that follows is fear of God (5:11).

decisions.choice: all who heard: those present and those who heard the news later
decisions.reason: The present participle can cover both. 5:11 says the fear spread to all who heard of these things.

source.text: ἀναστάντες δὲ οἱ νεώτεροι συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν.

records.literal_gloss: Having arisen then the younger [ones] wrapped up him and having carried out buried [him].

en.L: And the younger men got up, wrapped him up, and carrying [him] out, buried [him].
en.B: The young men stood up, wound him in a cloth, carried him out and buried him.
en.R: Some young men got up and wrapped his body in cloth. They carried him out and buried him.

es.L: Y levantándose los jóvenes, lo envolvieron y, sacándo[lo], [lo] sepultaron.
es.B: Los jóvenes se levantaron, lo envolvieron en un lienzo, lo sacaron y lo enterraron.
es.R: Algunos jóvenes se levantaron y envolvieron el cuerpo en una tela. Lo sacaron y lo enterraron.

fr.L: Et les jeunes gens se levèrent, l’enveloppèrent, et [l’]emportant dehors, [l’]enterrèrent.
fr.B: Les jeunes hommes se levèrent, l’enveloppèrent d’un linceul, l’emportèrent et l’enterrèrent.
fr.R: Des jeunes hommes se sont levés et ont enveloppé son corps dans un tissu. Ils l’ont emporté dehors et ils l’ont enterré.

sw.L: Na vijana wakainuka, wakamzungushia [nguo], na wakimtoa nje, wakamzika.
sw.B: Vijana walisimama, wakamzungushia sanda, wakamtoa nje, wakamzika.
sw.R: Vijana fulani walisimama wakaufunga mwili wake kwa kitambaa. Wakamtoa nje, wakamzika.

decisions.choice: the younger men: young men of the community
decisions.reason: The word means simply the younger ones. 5:10 uses another word for young men. There is no sign of a set office.

decisions.choice: wrapped him up: covered or wound the body
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw together or wrap up, here preparing the body for burial.

decisions.choice: buried him: burial on the same day
decisions.reason: Jews usually buried the dead on the day they died, outside the city. Here it happens before his wife even knows (5:7).

decisions.choice: in a cloth (B); in cloth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he was wrapped in, as burial customs imply.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ὡρῶν τριῶν διάστημα καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μὴ εἰδυῖα τὸ γεγονὸς εἰσῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: It came to pass now about hours three interval, and the wife of him not knowing the having happened came in.

en.L: And there was an interval of about three hours, and his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
en.B: Some three hours later his wife arrived, unaware of what had taken place.
en.R: About three hours later, Ananias's wife came in. She did not know what had happened to her husband.

es.L: Y pasó un intervalo de unas tres horas, y su esposa entró, sin saber lo que había sucedido.
es.B: Unas tres horas más tarde llegó su esposa, sin saber lo que había pasado.
es.R: Unas tres horas después, la esposa de Ananías entró. Ella no sabía lo que le había pasado a su esposo.

fr.L: Et il y eut un intervalle d’environ trois heures, et sa femme entra, sans savoir ce qui était arrivé.
fr.B: Environ trois heures plus tard, sa femme arriva, sans rien savoir de ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Environ trois heures plus tard, la femme d’Ananias est entrée. Elle ne savait pas ce qui était arrivé à son mari.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya muda wa kama saa tatu, mkewe akaingia, bila kujua yaliyotokea.
sw.B: Baada ya kama saa tatu hivi, mkewe alifika, bila kujua yaliyokuwa yametokea.
sw.R: Baada ya kama saa tatu, mke wa Anania aliingia. Hakujua yaliyompata mumewe.

decisions.choice: not knowing: no one had told her
decisions.reason: She comes in without knowing her husband is dead, so Peter's question gives her a chance to tell the truth (5:8).

decisions.choice: came in: to where Peter and the believers were
decisions.reason: Peter is there to speak to her (5:8).

decisions.choice: to her husband
decisions.reason: Readable says whom it had happened to.

decisions.choice: saa tatu (three hours)
decisions.reason: Here the Greek counts a length of time, not the hour of the day, so "saa tatu" means three hours, not nine in the morning.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν Πέτρος· Εἰπέ μοι, εἰ τοσούτου τὸ χωρίον ἀπέδοσθε;

records.literal_gloss: Answered then to her Peter, Tell me, if for so much the land you sold?

en.L: And Peter answered her, "Tell me whether you sold the land for so much."
en.B: Peter said to her, "Tell me, did the two of you sell the land for this amount?"
en.R: Peter asked her, "Tell me, is this how much money you and your husband got for the land?"

es.L: Y Pedro le respondió: «Dime si {{plural_you:vendieron|vendisteis}} el terreno por tanto».
es.B: Pedro le preguntó: «Dime, ¿{{plural_you:vendieron ustedes dos|vendisteis vosotros dos}} el terreno por esta cantidad?».
es.R: Pedro le preguntó: «Dime, ¿es esta la cantidad de dinero que tú y tu esposo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} por el terreno?».

fr.L: Et Pierre lui répondit : « Dis-moi si c’est pour tant que vous avez vendu le terrain. »
fr.B: Pierre lui dit : « Dis-moi, est-ce pour cette somme que vous avez vendu le terrain ? »
fr.R: Pierre lui a demandé : « Dis-moi, est-ce que c’est l’argent que ton mari et toi avez reçu pour le terrain ? »

sw.L: Na Petro akamjibu, "Niambie kama mliuza kiwanja kwa kiasi hiki."
sw.B: Petro alimwuliza, "Niambie, je, ninyi wawili mliuza kiwanja kwa kiasi hiki?"
sw.R: Petro alimwuliza, "Niambie, je, hiki ndicho kiasi cha fedha ambacho wewe na mumeo mlipata kwa kiwanja?"

decisions.choice: answered: spoke in response to her coming
decisions.reason: No one has asked anything. As in 3:12, the verb means he spoke up.

decisions.choice: you sold: you two, the plural
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. Peter asks about what she and Ananias did together.

decisions.choice: for so much: the sum Ananias had brought
decisions.reason: Peter likely points to the money laid at his feet, or names it. Either way she is asked to confirm the false price.

decisions.choice: the two of you (B); you and your husband (R)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural, so Balanced and Readable spell it out.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Peter speaks to Sapphira but uses the plural, meaning her and her husband (meaning decision m2). Each plural "you" and its verb in this chapter is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: vous avez vendu, without "tous les deux"
alternatives: vous avez vendu tous les deux
decisions.reason: English Balanced adds "the two of you" because English "you" does not show the plural (m2). French "vous", beside the "tu" of "Dis-moi", already shows it; Readable still names her husband, for clarity.

source.text: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, τοσούτου.

records.literal_gloss: She and said, Yes, for so much.

en.L: And she said, "Yes, for so much."
en.B: "Yes," she replied, "that was the price."
en.R: She said, "Yes, that is how much."

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Sí, por tanto».
es.B: «Sí —respondió ella—, ese fue el precio».
es.R: Ella dijo: «Sí, esa es la cantidad».

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Oui, pour tant. »
fr.B: « Oui, répondit-elle, c’était bien le prix. »
fr.R: Elle a dit : « Oui, c’est cette somme-là. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Ndiyo, kwa kiasi hicho."
sw.B: "Ndiyo," akajibu, "hiyo ndiyo bei."
sw.R: Akasema, "Ndiyo, ni kiasi hicho."

decisions.choice: she repeats the lie in her own words
decisions.reason: Given the chance to speak the truth, she confirms the false price. Peter's next words (5:9) say they had agreed on it together.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν· Τί ὅτι συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν πειράσαι τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου;

records.literal_gloss: The but Peter [said] to her, Why that it was agreed by you to test the Spirit of Lord?

en.L: And Peter [said] to her, "Why is it that you agreed together to test the Spirit of [the] Lord?
en.B: Peter said to her, "Why did the two of you agree together to put the Spirit of the Lord to the test?
en.R: Then Peter said to her, "Why did you and your husband plan together to test the Lord's Spirit like this?

es.L: Y Pedro [dijo] a ella: «¿Por qué se acordó entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tentar al Espíritu [del] Señor?
es.B: Pedro le dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:se pusieron|os pusisteis}} de acuerdo los dos para poner a prueba al Espíritu del Señor?
es.R: Entonces Pedro le dijo: «¿Por qué tú y tu esposo {{plural_you:planearon|planeasteis}} juntos poner a prueba así al Espíritu del Señor?

fr.L: Et Pierre [lui dit] : « Pourquoi vous êtes-vous mis d’accord pour mettre à l’épreuve l’Esprit du Seigneur ?
fr.B: Pierre lui dit : « Pourquoi vous êtes-vous entendus pour mettre à l’épreuve l’Esprit du Seigneur ?
fr.R: Alors Pierre lui a dit : « Pourquoi ton mari et toi, vous êtes-vous mis d’accord pour mettre ainsi à l’épreuve l’Esprit du Seigneur ?

sw.L: Na Petro [akasema] kwake, "Imekuwaje mkakubaliana kumjaribu Roho wa Bwana?
sw.B: Petro akamwambia, "Kwa nini ninyi wawili mlikubaliana kumjaribu Roho wa Bwana?
sw.R: Kisha Petro akamwambia, "Kwa nini wewe na mumeo mlipanga pamoja kumjaribu Roho wa Bwana namna hii?

decisions.choice: to test: to try God's patience, as Israel did in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Israel tested God at Massah (Exodus 17:2, 17:7), and the law says, "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test" (Deuteronomy 6:16; Luke 4:12). Ananias and Sapphira acted as if the Spirit would not see.

decisions.choice: agreed together: made a shared plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to sound together, to come to an agreement. It confirms 5:2.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the Lord: the Holy Spirit of 5:3
decisions.reason: The Lord may be God, as in Luke 4:18, which quotes Isaiah, or the Lord Jesus, as in 16:7, where the Spirit is called "the Spirit of Jesus". The Spirit is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the two of you (B); you and your husband (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8, English needs to show the plural.

decisions.choice: tentar (L); poner a prueba (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the verb of the old Spanish wording of Israel testing God in the wilderness (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say plainly what it means, to see how far God will let them go.

source.text: ἰδοὺ οἱ πόδες τῶν θαψάντων τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ καὶ ἐξοίσουσίν σε.

records.literal_gloss: Behold the feet of those having buried the husband of you [are] at the door, and they will carry out you.

en.L: Look, the feet of those who buried your husband [are] at the door, and they will carry you out."
en.B: Look, the men who buried your husband are already at the door. They will carry you out as well."
en.R: The men who just buried your husband are at the door. They will carry you out too."

es.L: Mira, los pies de los que sepultaron a tu esposo [están] a la puerta, y te sacarán».
es.B: Mira, los que sepultaron a tu esposo ya están a la puerta. También a ti te sacarán».
es.R: Los hombres que acaban de enterrar a tu esposo están a la puerta. También te sacarán a ti».

fr.L: Voici, les pieds de ceux qui ont enterré ton mari [sont] à la porte, et ils t’emporteront. »
fr.B: Écoute : les hommes qui ont enterré ton mari sont déjà à la porte. Ils vont t’emporter, toi aussi. »
fr.R: Les hommes qui viennent d’enterrer ton mari sont à la porte. Ils vont t’emporter, toi aussi. »

sw.L: Tazama, miguu ya wale waliomzika mumeo [iko] mlangoni, nao watakutoa nje."
sw.B: Tazama, wale waliomzika mumeo tayari wako mlangoni. Watakutoa nje wewe pia."
sw.R: Watu waliomzika mumeo sasa hivi wako mlangoni. Watakutoa nje wewe pia."

decisions.choice: the feet are at the door: they are arriving now
alternatives: only their footsteps can be heard
decisions.reason: "Feet" stands for the people coming. They are just back from the burial, about three hours after it began (5:7).

decisions.choice: they will carry you out: Peter foretells her death
alternatives: a threat of punishment by the believers
decisions.reason: Peter speaks as a prophet. He does not strike her down; he says what God will do, and it happens at once (5:10).

decisions.choice: the men who buried your husband are at the door
alternatives: the feet of those who buried
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "feet".

source.text: ἔπεσεν δὲ παραχρῆμα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξέψυξεν· εἰσελθόντες δὲ οἱ νεανίσκοι εὗρον αὐτὴν νεκράν, καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: She fell then at once at the feet of him and breathed out; having come in then the young men found her dead, and having carried out they buried [her] beside the husband of her.

en.L: And immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last; and the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying [her] out, they buried [her] beside her husband.
en.B: Instantly she collapsed at Peter's feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, and carried her out to bury her next to her husband.
en.R: Right away she fell down at Peter's feet and died. The young men came in and saw that she was dead. They carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

es.L: Y al instante cayó a sus pies y expiró; y entrando los jóvenes, la encontraron muerta, y sacándo[la], [la] sepultaron junto a su esposo.
es.B: Al instante se desplomó a los pies de Pedro y murió. Los jóvenes entraron, la encontraron muerta y la sacaron para enterrarla junto a su esposo.
es.R: En ese mismo momento cayó a los pies de Pedro y murió. Los jóvenes entraron y vieron que estaba muerta. La sacaron y la enterraron junto a su esposo.

fr.L: Et aussitôt elle tomba à ses pieds et expira ; et les jeunes gens, étant entrés, la trouvèrent morte, et [l’]emportant dehors, ils [l’]enterrèrent auprès de son mari.
fr.B: Au même instant, elle s’effondra aux pieds de Pierre et mourut. Les jeunes hommes entrèrent, la trouvèrent morte et l’emportèrent pour l’enterrer auprès de son mari.
fr.R: Tout de suite, elle est tombée aux pieds de Pierre et elle est morte. Les jeunes hommes sont entrés et ils ont vu qu’elle était morte. Ils l’ont emportée et l’ont enterrée à côté de son mari.

sw.L: Na mara moja akaanguka miguuni pake, akakata roho; na vijana walipoingia wakamkuta amekufa, na wakimtoa nje, wakamzika kando ya mumewe.
sw.B: Mara moja alianguka miguuni pa Petro, akafa. Vijana walipoingia walimkuta amekufa, wakamtoa nje, wakamzika kando ya mumewe.
sw.R: Papo hapo alianguka miguuni pa Petro, akafa. Vijana walipoingia waliona kwamba amekufa. Wakamtoa nje, wakamzika kando ya mumewe.

decisions.choice: at his feet: where the money had been laid
decisions.reason: The gift was laid "at the feet of the apostles" (5:2); now she falls at Peter's feet. Luke tells it so that the two scenes answer each other.

decisions.choice: breathed her last: died
decisions.reason: The same verb as of Ananias (5:5).

decisions.choice: the young men: the same group as in 5:6
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different word, but they are the younger men who buried Ananias.

decisions.choice: Peter's feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Peter.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: And came fear great upon whole the church and upon all those hearing these things.

en.L: And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.
en.B: The entire church was filled with deep fear, as was everyone who heard about these things.
en.R: All the believers in the church were very afraid. So was everyone else who heard about what had happened.

es.L: Y vino un gran temor sobre toda la iglesia y sobre todos los que oían estas cosas.
es.B: Un profundo temor se apoderó de toda la iglesia y de todos los que oyeron hablar de estas cosas.
es.R: Todos los creyentes de la iglesia sintieron mucho miedo. Y también todos los demás que oyeron lo que había pasado.

fr.L: Et une grande crainte s’empara de toute l’Église et de tous ceux qui apprenaient ces choses.
fr.B: Une crainte profonde saisit l’Église tout entière, ainsi que tous ceux qui apprirent ces événements.
fr.R: Tous les croyants de l’Église ont eu très peur. Tous les autres qui ont appris ce qui s’était passé ont eu peur aussi.

sw.L: Na hofu kuu ikaja juu ya kanisa lote na juu ya wote waliosikia mambo haya.
sw.B: Kanisa lote lilijawa na hofu kubwa, pamoja na wote waliosikia habari za mambo hayo.
sw.R: Waumini wote wa kanisa waliogopa sana. Vivyo hivyo na watu wengine wote waliosikia yaliyotokea.

decisions.choice: the church: the community of those who believe in Jesus, God's people gathered together
decisions.reason: This is the word's first use in Acts. It means an assembly of people called together. The Greek Old Testament uses it for Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10, 31:30), and Stephen uses it so of Israel in the wilderness (7:38). In 19:32-41 it is a town's assembly. Here it names the believers as one body (8:1, 9:31). It means people, not a building.

decisions.choice: fear: dread and awe of God
decisions.reason: As in 2:43 and 9:31, the fear is a deep reverence for God, who had shown that he could not be deceived.

decisions.choice: all who heard: those outside the church as well
decisions.reason: "And upon all" adds people beyond the church. 5:13 shows the effect on outsiders.

decisions.choice: church
decisions.reason: "Church" is the English word for this community of believers, as the meaning note explains. "Assembly" is kept for the places where the word means another gathering (7:38, 19:32-41).

decisions.choice: all the believers in the church
decisions.reason: Readable says that the church is the believers.

decisions.choice: la iglesia
decisions.reason: The community of those who believe in Jesus (meaning decision m1), the word used for it across the New Testament drafts; this is its first use in Acts.

decisions.choice: l'Église, capitalised (for the whole chapter)
alternatives: l'église, as for one local congregation
decisions.reason: The style guide (§9) writes "l'Église" for the whole body of believers and "l'église" for one congregation. Here the believers in Jerusalem are, at this point, the whole church, and Luke calls it simply "the whole church" (m1), so the capital is used. A reviewer may prefer the lowercase as for a local community.

decisions.choice: kanisa
decisions.reason: The community of those who believe in Jesus (meaning decision m1), the word used for it across the New Testament drafts; this is its first use in Acts.

source.text: Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πολλὰ ἐν τῷ λαῷ· καὶ ἦσαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἅπαντες ἐν τῇ Στοᾷ Σολομῶντος·

records.literal_gloss: Through now the hands of the apostles were happening signs and wonders many among the people; and they were with one accord all in the Porch of Solomon,

en.L: And through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were happening among the people; and they were all with one mind in Solomon's Porch.
en.B: By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders kept taking place among the people. With one mind, the believers all gathered in Solomon's Porch.
en.R: God used the apostles to do many signs and wonders among the people. All the believers met together at Solomon's Porch, a covered walkway in the temple courts.

es.L: Y por medio de las manos de los apóstoles sucedían muchas señales y prodigios en el pueblo; y todos estaban de un mismo sentir en el Pórtico de Salomón.
es.B: Por manos de los apóstoles se realizaban muchas señales y prodigios entre el pueblo. Con un mismo sentir, los creyentes se reunían todos en el Pórtico de Salomón.
es.R: Dios usaba a los apóstoles para hacer muchas señales y maravillas entre la gente. Todos los creyentes se reunían en el Pórtico de Salomón, un pasillo con techo en los patios del templo.

fr.L: Et par les mains des apôtres se produisaient beaucoup de signes et de prodiges parmi le peuple ; et ils étaient tous d’un même cœur au Portique de Salomon.
fr.B: Par les mains des apôtres, beaucoup de signes et de prodiges s’accomplissaient parmi le peuple. D’un même cœur, les croyants se réunissaient tous sous le Portique de Salomon.
fr.R: Dieu se servait des apôtres pour faire beaucoup de signes et de prodiges parmi le peuple. Tous les croyants se réunissaient au Portique de Salomon, une galerie couverte dans les cours du temple.

sw.L: Na kwa mikono ya mitume ishara na maajabu mengi yalikuwa yakitendeka kati ya watu; nao wote walikuwa na nia moja katika Ukumbi wa Sulemani.
sw.B: Kwa mikono ya mitume ishara nyingi na maajabu yalitendeka kati ya watu. Waumini wote walikutana kwa nia moja katika Ukumbi wa Sulemani.
sw.R: Mungu aliwatumia mitume kufanya ishara nyingi na maajabu kati ya watu. Waumini wote walikutana pamoja katika Ukumbi wa Sulemani, njia ndefu yenye paa katika nyua za hekalu.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: astonishing works that point to God
decisions.reason: The believers had prayed for this in 4:30. The same pair describes the works of Jesus (2:22) and of the apostles (2:43).

decisions.choice: through the hands of the apostles: God working through them
alternatives: only by laying on of hands
decisions.reason: "Hands" stands for what a person does. The believers asked God to stretch out his hand to heal (4:30).

decisions.choice: they all: the believers, or the apostles
decisions.reason: The last people named are the apostles. But "all" and "with one mind" are used of the whole community (2:46, 4:24), and 5:13 contrasts them with "the rest".

decisions.choice: Solomon's Porch: the roofed colonnade on the east side of the temple's outer court
decisions.reason: As in 3:11.

decisions.choice: God used the apostles to do
alternatives: through the hands of the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one at work, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" most likely are, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: señales y prodigios (L, B); señales y maravillas (R)
decisions.reason: "Milagros" would lose the two sides of the pair: works that point to God and works that amaze (meaning decision m1). Readable uses the commoner "maravillas".

decisions.choice: ishara na maajabu
decisions.reason: "Ishara" is the word for a sign that points to God, never "muujiza" (miracle), and "maajabu" are wonders that amaze, so the pair keeps both sides of the Greek (meaning decision m1).

source.text: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ’ ἐμεγάλυνεν αὐτοὺς ὁ λαός, μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο πιστεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ πλήθη ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Of the but rest no one was daring to join them, but were magnifying them the people; \v 14 more and were being added believing to the Lord, multitudes of men both and of women,

en.L: But of the rest no one dared to join them, but the people held them in high honor; \v 14 and more than ever believers were added to the Lord, crowds of both men and women,
en.B: None of the others dared to associate with them, yet the people thought highly of them. \v 14 Still more believers were brought to the Lord, great numbers of men and women alike.
en.R: Other people were afraid to join the believers, but everyone spoke well of them. \v 14 More and more people believed and became followers of the Lord. Many men and many women joined them.

es.L: Pero de los demás nadie se atrevía a juntarse con ellos, pero el pueblo los tenía en gran estima; \v 14 y más aún se añadían creyentes al Señor, multitudes tanto de hombres como de mujeres,
es.B: Ninguno de los demás se atrevía a unirse a ellos, aunque el pueblo los tenía en alta estima. \v 14 Y cada vez se sumaban más creyentes al Señor, gran cantidad de hombres y también de mujeres.
es.R: Otras personas tenían miedo de unirse a los creyentes, pero todos hablaban bien de ellos. \v 14 Cada vez más personas creían y se hacían seguidores del Señor. Muchos hombres y muchas mujeres se unieron a ellos.

fr.L: Mais des autres, personne n’osait se joindre à eux, mais le peuple les tenait en haute estime ; \v 14 et plus que jamais des croyants étaient ajoutés au Seigneur, des foules d’hommes et de femmes,
fr.B: Aucun des autres n’osait se joindre à eux, et pourtant le peuple les estimait beaucoup. \v 14 Des croyants de plus en plus nombreux s’attachaient au Seigneur, des foules d’hommes et de femmes.
fr.R: Les autres avaient peur de se joindre aux croyants, mais tout le monde disait du bien d’eux. \v 14 De plus en plus de gens croyaient et devenaient disciples du Seigneur. Beaucoup d’hommes et beaucoup de femmes les ont rejoints.

sw.L: Lakini katika wale wengine hakuna aliyethubutu kujiunga nao, bali watu waliwaheshimu sana; \v 14 na zaidi waliongezwa kwa Bwana watu walioamini, wingi wa wanaume na wa wanawake,
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja wa wale wengine aliyethubutu kujiunga nao, ingawa watu waliwasifu sana. \v 14 Waumini wengi zaidi waliletwa kwa Bwana, idadi kubwa ya wanaume na wanawake pia.
sw.R: Watu wengine waliogopa kujiunga na waumini, lakini kila mtu aliwasifu. \v 14 Watu wengi zaidi na zaidi waliamini, wakawa wafuasi wa Bwana. Wanaume wengi na wanawake wengi walijiunga nao.

decisions.choice: the rest: people outside the believers
alternatives: the rest of the believers, who kept apart from the apostles
decisions.reason: After what happened to Ananias and Sapphira, no one joined the believers lightly. Yet many did join who truly believed (5:14). Some read "the rest" as other believers who held back from the apostles.

decisions.choice: join: to attach oneself closely to a group
decisions.reason: The verb means to be glued or joined to. 9:26 and 10:28 use it for associating with people.

decisions.choice: held them in high honor: praised them
decisions.reason: The verb means to make great, so to speak highly of.

decisions.choice: added to the Lord: brought into the Lord's people by believing
alternatives: believing in the Lord, they were added (to the church)
decisions.reason: The words "to the Lord" can go with "were added" or with "believing". 11:24 says a great crowd "was added to the Lord", and 2:47 says the Lord added to their number. Either way, they believed in the Lord and joined his people.

decisions.choice: both men and women: Luke names both
decisions.reason: Luke often names women alongside men among the believers (8:3, 8:12, 17:4, 17:12).

decisions.choice: believed and became followers of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what being added to the Lord means.

source.text: ὥστε καὶ εἰς τὰς πλατείας ἐκφέρειν τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς καὶ τιθέναι ἐπὶ κλιναρίων καὶ κραβάττων, ἵνα ἐρχομένου Πέτρου κἂν ἡ σκιὰ ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: so that even into the streets to carry out the sick and to put on cots and mats, so that coming Peter at least the shadow might overshadow some of them.

en.L: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid [them] on cots and mats, so that when Peter came by, at least [his] shadow might fall on some of them.
en.B: People would even carry their sick out into the streets and lay them on cots and pallets, hoping that when Peter came along, his shadow, if nothing more, might fall across some of them.
en.R: People even carried sick people out into the streets. They put them on beds and mats. They hoped that when Peter walked by, his shadow would at least touch some of them.

es.L: de modo que incluso sacaban a los enfermos a las calles y [los] ponían sobre catres y camillas, para que, al pasar Pedro, al menos [su] sombra cubriera a alguno de ellos.
es.B: La gente llegaba a sacar a sus enfermos a las calles y a ponerlos en catres y camillas, con la esperanza de que, al pasar Pedro, cayera sobre alguno de ellos aunque solo fuera su sombra.
es.R: La gente incluso sacaba a los enfermos a las calles. Los ponían en camas y camillas. Esperaban que, cuando Pedro pasara, por lo menos su sombra tocara a algunos de ellos.

fr.L: si bien qu’on portait même les malades dans les rues et qu’on [les] plaçait sur des lits et des nattes, afin que, quand Pierre passerait, au moins [son] ombre couvre l’un d’eux.
fr.B: On allait jusqu’à sortir les malades dans les rues pour les coucher sur des lits et des brancards, dans l’espoir que, lorsque Pierre passerait, son ombre au moins tombe sur certains d’entre eux.
fr.R: Les gens allaient même jusqu’à porter des malades dans les rues. Ils les mettaient sur des lits et des nattes. Ils espéraient que, quand Pierre passerait, son ombre toucherait au moins certains d’entre eux.

sw.L: hata wakawatoa wagonjwa nje barabarani na kuwaweka juu ya vitanda vidogo na mikeka, ili Petro akipita, angalau kivuli [chake] kiwafunike baadhi yao.
sw.B: Watu walifikia hata kuwaleta wagonjwa wao barabarani na kuwalaza juu ya vitanda na machela, wakitumaini kwamba Petro akipita, angalau kivuli chake kiwaangukie baadhi yao.
sw.R: Watu waliwaleta hata wagonjwa barabarani. Waliwalaza juu ya vitanda na machela. Walitumaini kwamba Petro akipita, angalau kivuli chake kingewagusa baadhi yao.

decisions.choice: so that: the result of the signs in 5:12
decisions.reason: 5:12b-14 is an aside about the believers; "so that" picks up the signs done by the apostles. It may also follow from the growth just described.

decisions.choice: cots and mats: beds that could be carried
decisions.reason: The first word is a small bed; the second is a poor person's mat or pallet, as in Mark 2:4.

decisions.choice: his shadow at least: the people's hope of healing
decisions.reason: Luke reports what people hoped, as with the woman who touched Jesus's clothes (Luke 8:44) and the cloths taken from Paul (19:12). 5:16 says that all were healed, so God honored their faith.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence ends here
alternatives: some manuscripts add "and they were set free from every sickness they had"
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and some other witnesses add words saying the sick were freed from their illnesses. The SBLGNT, with most manuscripts, does not have them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if nothing more
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "at least" in a way that reads naturally after "his shadow".

decisions.choice: catres y camillas (L, B); camas y camillas (R)
decisions.reason: Both were beds that could be carried (meaning decision m2). "Camilla" is the word used for the second across the New Testament drafts; "catre" is a light, low bed.

decisions.choice: vitanda vidogo na mikeka (L); vitanda na machela (B, R)
decisions.reason: Both were beds that could be carried (meaning decision m2). For the second word the New Testament drafts say "mkeka" (a sleeping mat) at Literal and "machela" (a stretcher) at Balanced and Readable, where the sick are carried on it.

source.text: συνήρχετο δὲ καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πέριξ πόλεων Ἰερουσαλήμ, φέροντες ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ὀχλουμένους ὑπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων, οἵτινες ἐθεραπεύοντο ἅπαντες.

records.literal_gloss: Were coming together now also the multitude of the around cities of Jerusalem, bringing sick and being troubled by spirits unclean, who were being healed all.

en.L: And the crowd from the towns around Jerusalem also came together, bringing [the] sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, who were all healed.
en.B: People streamed in, too, from the towns near Jerusalem. They brought those who were sick or harassed by unclean spirits, and every one of them was made well.
en.R: Large crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought people who were sick and people who were troubled by evil spirits. And all of them were healed.

es.L: Y también se juntaba la multitud de los pueblos de alrededor de Jerusalén, trayendo enfermos y atormentados por espíritus impuros, los cuales eran sanados todos.
es.B: También acudía mucha gente de los pueblos cercanos a Jerusalén. Traían a los que estaban enfermos o atormentados por espíritus impuros, y todos eran sanados.
es.R: También llegaban muchas personas de los pueblos alrededor de Jerusalén. Traían a gente enferma y a gente atormentada por espíritus malignos. Y todos eran sanados.

fr.L: Et la foule des villes autour de Jérusalem accourait aussi, apportant des malades et des [gens] tourmentés par des esprits impurs, qui étaient tous guéris.
fr.B: Des gens affluaient aussi des villes voisines de Jérusalem. Ils amenaient des malades et des personnes harcelées par des esprits impurs, et tous sans exception étaient guéris.
fr.R: De grandes foules venaient aussi des villes autour de Jérusalem. Elles amenaient des malades et des gens tourmentés par des esprits mauvais. Et tous étaient guéris.

sw.L: Na wingi wa watu wa miji ya kuzunguka Yerusalemu pia walikuwa wakikusanyika, wakiwaleta wagonjwa na wale walioteswa na pepo wachafu, nao wote walikuwa wakiponywa.
sw.B: Watu wengi walimiminika pia kutoka miji iliyo karibu na Yerusalemu. Waliwaleta wagonjwa na wale waliosumbuliwa na pepo wachafu, na wote waliponywa.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa pia ulikuja kutoka miji iliyozunguka Yerusalemu. Waliwaleta watu wagonjwa na watu walioteswa na pepo wabaya. Na wote waliponywa.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the towns around Jerusalem"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the towns around, to Jerusalem"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("the cities round about unto Jerusalem"), add "to", so that the crowds come into Jerusalem. The meaning is close. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Luke uses this name for demons (Luke 4:33, 4:36, 8:29). Those troubled by them are named apart from the sick.

decisions.choice: all were healed: no one went away unhealed
decisions.reason: As with Jesus (Luke 4:40, 6:19). The healing is God's doing (4:30).

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for spirits that are against God.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: Demons (meaning decision m2); the wording used for them across the New Testament drafts, with the plainer "malignos" at Readable, as the English "evil spirits".

decisions.choice: des esprits impurs (L, B); des esprits mauvais (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term (§9) at Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the plainer English "evil spirits".

decisions.choice: pepo wachafu (L, B); pepo wabaya (R)
decisions.reason: Demons (meaning decision m2). Swahili calls them "pepo", keeping "roho" for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit, as across the New Testament drafts; Readable says "wabaya" (evil), as the English "evil spirits".

source.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ πάντες οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ, ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτοὺς ἐν τηρήσει δημοσίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Having risen up but the high priest and all those with him, the being sect of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy \v 18 and laid the hands on the apostles and put them in custody public.

en.L: But the high priest rose up, and all those with him, that is, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy, \v 18 and they laid hands on the apostles and put them in [the] public jail.
en.B: But the high priest rose to act, and with him all who sided with him, the Sadducee party. Burning with jealousy, \v 18 they took hold of the apostles and shut them up in the public prison.
en.R: The high priest and his friends, the Sadducees, became very jealous of the apostles. So they decided to act. \v 18 They arrested the apostles and put them in the city jail.

es.L: Pero levantándose el sumo sacerdote y todos los que [estaban] con él, que eran el partido de los saduceos, se llenaron de celos \v 18 y echaron mano a los apóstoles y los pusieron en [la] cárcel pública.
es.B: Pero el sumo sacerdote se levantó para actuar, y con él todos los de su lado, el partido de los saduceos. Llenos de celos, \v 18 apresaron a los apóstoles y los encerraron en la cárcel pública.
es.R: El sumo sacerdote y sus amigos, los saduceos, sintieron muchos celos de los apóstoles. Así que decidieron actuar. \v 18 Arrestaron a los apóstoles y los metieron en la cárcel de la ciudad.

fr.L: Mais le grand prêtre se leva, ainsi que tous ceux qui étaient avec lui, c’est-à-dire le parti des Sadducéens, et ils furent remplis de jalousie, \v 18 et ils mirent les mains sur les apôtres et les placèrent dans la prison publique.
fr.B: Mais le grand prêtre passa à l’action, et avec lui tous ceux de son camp, le parti des Sadducéens. Brûlant de jalousie, \v 18 ils se saisirent des apôtres et les enfermèrent dans la prison publique.
fr.R: Le grand prêtre et ses amis, les Sadducéens, sont devenus très jaloux des apôtres. Alors ils ont décidé d’agir. \v 18 Ils ont arrêté les apôtres et les ont mis dans la prison de la ville.

sw.L: Lakini kuhani mkuu akainuka, na wote waliokuwa pamoja naye, yaani kundi la Masadukayo, wakajaa wivu, \v 18 wakaweka mikono juu ya mitume, wakawatia katika gereza la umma.
sw.B: Lakini kuhani mkuu aliinuka kuchukua hatua, pamoja na wote waliokuwa upande wake, yaani kundi la Masadukayo. Wakiwa wamejaa wivu, \v 18 waliwakamata mitume na kuwafunga katika gereza la umma.
sw.R: Kuhani mkuu na rafiki zake, Masadukayo, waliwaonea mitume wivu sana. Kwa hiyo wakaamua kuchukua hatua. \v 18 Waliwakamata mitume, wakawatia katika gereza la mji.

decisions.choice: rose up: took action
decisions.reason: The verb is used of someone setting out to do something, as in 5:34 and 5:36.

decisions.choice: the high priest: the head of the temple and of the council
decisions.reason: Caiaphas held the office in these years; Luke also calls his father-in-law Annas high priest (4:6; Luke 3:2; John 18:13). Which one is meant here is not said.

decisions.choice: the party of the Sadducees: a group of leading priestly families
alternatives: a sect cut off from Judaism
decisions.reason: The Sadducees held the high priesthood and much power in the temple. They said there is no resurrection, no angel and no spirit (23:8; Luke 20:27). They were angry that the apostles proclaimed the resurrection in Jesus (4:1-2). "Party" has no bad sense here; Luke uses the same word of the Pharisees (15:5).

decisions.choice: jealousy: resentment at the apostles' success
decisions.reason: The word can mean zeal, but here, as in 13:45, it is jealousy at the crowds who honored the apostles (5:13-16).

decisions.choice: the public jail: the city's prison
decisions.reason: A jail kept by the authorities, as in 4:3. All the apostles were held this time, not just Peter and John.

decisions.choice: jealous of the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they were jealous of.

decisions.choice: el partido de los saduceos
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a group or party within the people (meaning decision m3). In Spanish today "secta" suggests a cult cut off from others, which the Sadducees, the leading priestly families, were not.

decisions.choice: kundi la Masadukayo
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a group or party within the people (meaning decision m3). "Dhehebu" today means a church denomination; "kundi" (group, party) says what the Sadducees were.

source.text: ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου διὰ νυκτὸς ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς ἐξαγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἶπεν·

records.literal_gloss: An angel but of Lord during night opened the doors of the prison, having brought out and them said,

en.L: But during the night an angel of [the] Lord opened the doors of the prison, and bringing them out, he said,
en.B: That night, though, an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison. He led them outside and said to them,
en.R: But that night an angel from the Lord opened the doors of the jail. He led the apostles out and said to them,

es.L: Pero un ángel del Señor, durante la noche, abrió las puertas de la cárcel, y sacándolos, dijo:
es.B: Pero esa noche un ángel del Señor abrió las puertas de la cárcel. Los sacó y les dijo:
es.R: Pero esa noche un ángel enviado por el Señor abrió las puertas de la cárcel. Sacó a los apóstoles y les dijo:

fr.L: Mais pendant la nuit, un ange du Seigneur ouvrit les portes de la prison, et les ayant fait sortir, il dit :
fr.B: Cette nuit-là, pourtant, un ange du Seigneur ouvrit les portes de la prison. Il les conduisit dehors et leur dit :
fr.R: Mais pendant la nuit, un ange envoyé par le Seigneur a ouvert les portes de la prison. Il a fait sortir les apôtres et il leur a dit :

sw.L: Lakini malaika wa Bwana wakati wa usiku akaifungua milango ya gereza, na akiwatoa nje akasema,
sw.B: Lakini usiku ule malaika wa Bwana alifungua milango ya gereza. Akawatoa nje, akawaambia,
sw.R: Lakini usiku ule malaika kutoka kwa Bwana alifungua milango ya gereza. Akawatoa mitume nje, akawaambia,

decisions.choice: an angel of the Lord: a messenger sent by God
decisions.reason: Angels of the Lord appear in Luke 1:11 and 2:9, and one frees Peter in 12:7-10. The Sadducees, who jailed the apostles, said there are no angels (23:8).

decisions.choice: during the night: in the course of that night
decisions.reason: The apostles were seized in the day and freed that same night; they are in the temple at dawn (5:21).

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names them.

source.text: Πορεύεσθε καὶ σταθέντες λαλεῖτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: Go and having stood speak in the temple to the people all the words of the life this.

en.L: "Go, and standing in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life."
en.B: "Go and take your stand in the temple, and tell the people the whole message of this life."
en.R: "Go to the temple. Stand there and tell the people everything about the life that Jesus gives."

es.L: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, y puestos de pie, {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} en el templo al pueblo todas las palabras de esta vida».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} de pie en el templo y {{plural_you:comuniquen|comunicad}} al pueblo todo el mensaje de esta vida».
es.R: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al templo. {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} de pie allí y {{plural_you:cuéntenle|contadle}} a la gente todo acerca de la vida que Jesús da».

fr.L: « Allez, et vous tenant dans le temple, dites au peuple toutes les paroles de cette vie. »
fr.B: « Allez vous tenir dans la cour du temple, et annoncez au peuple tout le message de cette vie. »
fr.R: « Allez dans la cour du temple. Restez là et dites aux gens tout ce qui concerne la vie que Jésus donne. »

sw.L: "Nendeni, na mkisimama hekaluni, waambieni watu maneno yote ya uzima huu."
sw.B: "Nendeni mkasimame hekaluni, mkawaambie watu ujumbe wote wa uzima huu."
sw.R: "Nendeni hekaluni. Simameni pale mkawaambie watu kila kitu kuhusu uzima ambao Yesu anautoa."

decisions.choice: the words of this life: the message of the life that comes through Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter has called Jesus the Author of life (3:15). In 13:26 Paul speaks of "the message of this salvation". "This life" is the life the apostles proclaim, the life the Sadducees deny.

decisions.choice: standing: take your place openly
decisions.reason: They are to stand up in public, in the very place they were arrested from. 5:25 reports them "standing" there.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts, where people gathered
decisions.reason: As in 2:46 and 3:1.

decisions.choice: the life that Jesus gives
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this life" is, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R), for the whole chapter
decisions.reason: The word means the temple area with its courts, where people gathered (m3), not the sanctuary; the style guide (§5) keeps "le temple" at Literal and says "la cour du temple" at Balanced and Readable. English Readable makes the same point with "temple courts".

decisions.choice: uzima
decisions.reason: The life that comes through Jesus (meaning decision m1). "Uzima" is life itself, the word for eternal life across the drafts; "maisha" would suggest a way of living or a lifetime.

source.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἰσῆλθον ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκον.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard now they entered at the dawn into the temple and were teaching.

en.L: And having heard [this], they went into the temple about daybreak and began teaching.
en.B: Hearing this, they went into the temple at first light and began to teach.
en.R: The apostles obeyed. Early the next morning they went into the temple courts and started teaching.

es.L: Y habiendo oído [esto], entraron al amanecer en el templo y enseñaban.
es.B: Al oír esto, entraron en el templo al despuntar el día y se pusieron a enseñar.
es.R: Los apóstoles obedecieron. Muy temprano a la mañana siguiente entraron en los patios del templo y comenzaron a enseñar.

fr.L: Et ayant entendu, ils entrèrent dans le temple vers l’aube et se mirent à enseigner.
fr.B: Après avoir entendu cela, ils entrèrent dans la cour du temple dès le point du jour et se mirent à enseigner.
fr.R: Les apôtres ont obéi. Tôt le lendemain matin, ils sont entrés dans la cour du temple et ils ont commencé à enseigner.

sw.L: Na waliposikia [hayo], waliingia hekaluni karibu na mapambazuko, wakawa wakifundisha.
sw.B: Waliposikia hayo, waliingia hekaluni alfajiri, wakaanza kufundisha.
sw.R: Mitume walitii. Asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata waliingia katika nyua za hekalu, wakaanza kufundisha.

decisions.choice: having heard: they did as the angel said
decisions.reason: They obeyed at once, as early in the day as they could.

decisions.choice: about daybreak: when the temple opened and people began to come
decisions.reason: The morning sacrifice was offered at dawn, and people came early to the temple courts (Luke 21:38).

decisions.choice: the apostles obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable says what their hearing led to.

source.text: Παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ συνεκάλεσαν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον ἀχθῆναι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Having arrived now the high priest and those with him called together the council and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to be brought them.

en.L: Now the high priest and those with him came and called together the council and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.
en.B: Meanwhile the high priest and his party arrived. They summoned the council together with all the elders of Israel, and sent orders to the prison to bring the apostles.
en.R: Meanwhile the high priest and his friends called together the council and all the elders of Israel. The council was the group of Jewish leaders who governed the people. Then they sent men to the jail to bring the apostles to them.

es.L: Y llegando el sumo sacerdote y los que [estaban] con él, convocaron al concilio y a todo el senado de los hijos de Israel, y enviaron a la cárcel para que fueran traídos.
es.B: Entretanto llegaron el sumo sacerdote y los de su partido. Convocaron al Consejo junto con todos los ancianos de Israel, y mandaron a la cárcel a buscar a los apóstoles.
es.R: Mientras tanto, el sumo sacerdote y sus amigos reunieron al Consejo Supremo y a todos los ancianos de Israel. El Consejo Supremo era el grupo de líderes judíos que gobernaban al pueblo. Luego enviaron hombres a la cárcel para que les trajeran a los apóstoles.

fr.L: Or le grand prêtre et ceux qui étaient avec lui arrivèrent et convoquèrent le Sanhédrin et tout le sénat des fils d’Israël, et envoyèrent [quelqu’un] à la prison pour qu’on les amène.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, le grand prêtre et son entourage arrivèrent. Ils convoquèrent le Sanhédrin avec tous les anciens d’Israël, et envoyèrent à la prison l’ordre d’amener les apôtres.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, le grand prêtre et ses amis ont réuni le grand conseil des Juifs et tous les anciens d’Israël. Le grand conseil était le groupe de chefs juifs qui dirigeaient le peuple. Puis ils ont envoyé des hommes à la prison pour qu’on leur amène les apôtres.

sw.L: Basi kuhani mkuu na wale waliokuwa pamoja naye walipofika, wakaliita baraza pamoja na kusanyiko lote la wazee wa wana wa Israeli, wakatuma gerezani ili waletwe.
sw.B: Wakati huo kuhani mkuu na wenzake walifika. Wakaitisha baraza pamoja na wazee wote wa Israeli, wakatuma watu gerezani kuwaleta mitume.
sw.R: Wakati huo kuhani mkuu na rafiki zake waliitisha mkutano wa baraza kuu na wazee wote wa Israeli. Baraza kuu lilikuwa kundi la viongozi wa Kiyahudi waliowatawala watu. Kisha wakatuma watu gerezani wawalete mitume kwao.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the Jewish high council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: It was made up of chief priests, elders and scribes, with the high priest presiding (4:5-6; Luke 22:66). Later Jewish writings give it seventy-one members. Under Roman rule it governed Jewish affairs.

decisions.choice: and all the senate: the council's own body of elders, or elders added to it
decisions.reason: "And" may explain the council, "that is, the whole senate", or add to it other respected elders. The Greek Old Testament speaks of "the senate of the sons of Israel" (Exodus 12:21). Either way, Luke stresses that the full leadership of Israel was there.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: An old name for the nation, as in Exodus.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel
alternatives: the senate of the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the senate was and use the plain name of the people; Literal keeps both words.

decisions.choice: the group of Jewish leaders who governed the people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the council was.

decisions.choice: el concilio (L), el Consejo (B), el Consejo Supremo (R); el senado (L), los ancianos de Israel (B, R)
decisions.reason: The council is the Sanhedrin (meaning decision m1), named with the words used for it across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 26:59. Literal keeps "senado" for the Greek word for a body of elders; Balanced and Readable say "los ancianos", as the English does.

decisions.choice: le Sanhédrin (L, B); le grand conseil des Juifs (R), for the whole chapter
decisions.reason: The style guide's term (§9). Readable explains it once, as the English does.

decisions.choice: baraza (L, B), baraza kuu (R); kusanyiko la wazee (L), wazee wote wa Israeli (B, R)
decisions.reason: The council is the Sanhedrin (meaning decision m1), named with the words used for it across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 26:59. Literal says "kusanyiko la wazee" for the Greek word for a body of elders; Balanced and Readable say "wazee", as the English does.

source.text: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται οὐχ εὗρον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, ἀναστρέψαντες δὲ ἀπήγγειλαν λέγοντες ὅτι Τὸ δεσμωτήριον εὕρομεν κεκλεισμένον ἐν πάσῃ ἀσφαλείᾳ καὶ τοὺς φύλακας ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν, ἀνοίξαντες δὲ ἔσω οὐδένα εὕρομεν.

records.literal_gloss: The but having arrived officers not found them in the prison; having returned then they reported \v 23 saying that, The prison we found shut with all security and the guards standing at the doors, having opened but inside no one we found.

en.L: But the officers who came did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported, \v 23 saying, "We found the prison shut with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened [them], we found no one inside."
en.B: The officers went, but they did not find the apostles in the prison. They came back with this report: \v 23 "The prison was shut and fully secured when we got there, and the guards were at their posts by the doors. But once we had opened up, we found nobody inside."
en.R: The men went to the jail, but the apostles were not there. So they went back and told the leaders, \v 23 "The jail was locked tight, and the guards were standing at the doors. But when we opened the doors, nobody was inside!"

es.L: Pero los alguaciles que llegaron no los encontraron en la cárcel, y regresando, informaron \v 23 diciendo: «Encontramos la cárcel cerrada con toda seguridad y a los guardias de pie a las puertas, pero al abrir[las], no encontramos a nadie dentro».
es.B: Los guardias del templo fueron, pero no encontraron a los apóstoles en la cárcel. Volvieron con este informe: \v 23 «Cuando llegamos, la cárcel estaba cerrada y bien asegurada, y los centinelas estaban en sus puestos junto a las puertas. Pero cuando abrimos, no encontramos a nadie dentro».
es.R: Los hombres fueron a la cárcel, pero los apóstoles no estaban allí. Así que volvieron y les dijeron a los líderes: \v 23 «La cárcel estaba bien cerrada, y los guardias estaban de pie junto a las puertas. ¡Pero cuando abrimos las puertas, no había nadie adentro!».

fr.L: Mais les gardes, étant arrivés, ne les trouvèrent pas dans la prison ; et ils revinrent et firent leur rapport, \v 23 disant : « Nous avons trouvé la prison fermée en toute sûreté et les gardiens debout aux portes, mais quand nous avons ouvert, nous n’avons trouvé personne à l’intérieur. »
fr.B: Les gardes y allèrent, mais ne trouvèrent pas les apôtres dans la prison. Ils revinrent faire ce rapport : \v 23 « Quand nous sommes arrivés, la prison était fermée et parfaitement verrouillée, et les gardiens étaient à leur poste devant les portes. Mais une fois que nous avons ouvert, nous n’avons trouvé personne à l’intérieur. »
fr.R: Les hommes sont allés à la prison, mais les apôtres n’étaient pas là. Ils sont donc revenus et ils ont dit aux chefs : \v 23 « La prison était bien fermée à clé, et les gardiens étaient debout devant les portes. Mais quand nous avons ouvert les portes, il n’y avait personne à l’intérieur ! »

sw.L: Lakini wale walinzi walipofika hawakuwakuta gerezani; wakarudi, wakatoa taarifa, \v 23 wakisema, "Tumelikuta gereza limefungwa kwa usalama wote na askari wa zamu wamesimama milangoni, lakini tulipofungua, hatukumkuta mtu yeyote ndani."
sw.B: Walinzi walikwenda, lakini hawakuwakuta mitume gerezani. Wakarudi na taarifa hii: \v 23 "Tulipofika tulikuta gereza limefungwa barabara, na askari walikuwa wamesimama zamuni milangoni. Lakini tulipofungua hatukumkuta mtu yeyote ndani."
sw.R: Watu hao walikwenda gerezani, lakini mitume hawakuwamo. Kwa hiyo walirudi, wakawaambia viongozi, \v 23 "Gereza lilikuwa limefungwa kabisa, na askari walikuwa wamesimama milangoni. Lakini tulipofungua milango, hapakuwa na mtu ndani!"

decisions.choice: the officers: the temple police, under the captain of the temple
decisions.reason: The word means attendants or officers. They serve the captain of the temple (5:26).

decisions.choice: locked and guarded, yet empty
decisions.reason: Everything was secure, and no one had seen anything. The report shows that the apostles were freed by God, not by a human plan.

decisions.choice: with all security: locked as firmly as it could be
decisions.reason: The phrase means fully secured.

decisions.choice: the apostles; the leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people the pronouns point to.

decisions.choice: los alguaciles (L), los guardias del templo (B); los guardias (L), los centinelas (B)
decisions.reason: The officers are the temple police (meaning decision m1), named as in John 7:32 and 18:3. Balanced calls the men at the prison doors "centinelas" so that the two groups are not both "guardias".

decisions.choice: walinzi (the officers); askari (the guards at the doors)
decisions.reason: The officers are the temple police (meaning decision m1), "walinzi wa hekalu" as in John 7:32 and 18:3; the men posted at the prison doors are "askari", so that the two groups are not confused.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὅ τε στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, διηπόρουν περὶ αὐτῶν τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο.

records.literal_gloss: As now they heard the words these, both the captain of the temple and the chief priests were perplexed about them, what might become this.

en.L: And when they heard these words, both the captain of the temple and the chief priests were at a loss about them, [as to] what this might come to.
en.B: The report left the captain of the temple and the chief priests puzzled about the apostles, unsure what all this would come to.
en.R: The captain of the temple guard and the leading priests heard this. They could not understand what had happened to the apostles. They wondered what would happen next.

es.L: Y cuando oyeron estas palabras, tanto el capitán del templo como los jefes de los sacerdotes estaban perplejos acerca de ellos, [sobre] qué vendría a ser esto.
es.B: Al oír el informe, el capitán del templo y los jefes de los sacerdotes quedaron desconcertados por lo de los apóstoles, sin saber en qué terminaría todo aquello.
es.R: El jefe de la guardia del templo y los jefes de los sacerdotes oyeron esto. No podían entender qué les había pasado a los apóstoles. Se preguntaban qué pasaría después.

fr.L: Et quand ils entendirent ces paroles, le commandant du temple et les chefs des prêtres furent dans l’embarras à leur sujet, [se demandant] ce que cela pourrait devenir.
fr.B: Ce rapport laissa le chef de la garde du temple et les chefs des prêtres perplexes au sujet des apôtres : ils ne savaient pas où tout cela mènerait.
fr.R: Le chef des gardes du temple et les chefs des prêtres ont entendu cela. Ils ne comprenaient pas ce qui était arrivé aux apôtres. Ils se demandaient ce qui allait se passer ensuite.

sw.L: Na waliposikia maneno haya, mkuu wa [walinzi wa] hekalu na wakuu wa makuhani walifadhaika juu yao, [wakijiuliza] jambo hili lingekuwaje.
sw.B: Taarifa hiyo iliwaacha mkuu wa walinzi wa hekalu na wakuu wa makuhani wakiwa wamefadhaika juu ya mitume, bila kujua mambo hayo yangeishia wapi.
sw.R: Mkuu wa walinzi wa hekalu na wakuu wa makuhani walisikia habari hiyo. Hawakuelewa yaliyowapata mitume. Walijiuliza ni nini kingetokea baadaye.

decisions.choice: the captain of the temple: the priest in charge of the temple police
decisions.reason: He kept order in the temple with his officers (4:1; Luke 22:4, 22:52). He ranked next to the high priest among the temple leaders.

decisions.choice: the chief priests: the high priest's family and the leading priests
decisions.reason: As in 4:6 and 4:23, those of the high-priestly families who led the temple.

decisions.choice: about them: about the apostles, or about these words
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural and may point to the apostles or to the reports. The sense is the same: they could not explain what had happened.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the captain of the temple and the chief priests"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "the high priest" (or "the priest") at the start
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "the high priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the captain of the temple guard; the leading priests
alternatives: the captain of the temple; the chief priests
decisions.reason: Readable says what the captain was in charge of, and uses a plainer word for "chief".

decisions.choice: el capitán del templo (L, B), el jefe de la guardia del templo (R); los jefes de los sacerdotes
decisions.reason: The priest in charge of the temple police (meaning decision m1); Readable says what he commanded, as the English "captain of the temple guard". The chief priests are "los jefes de los sacerdotes" at every level, as across the New Testament drafts.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres, at every level
alternatives: les prêtres principaux (R), as the English "leading priests"
decisions.reason: The style guide's term (§9) is already plain French, so Readable keeps it.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa [walinzi wa] hekalu (L), mkuu wa walinzi wa hekalu (B, R); wakuu wa makuhani
decisions.reason: The priest in charge of the temple police (meaning decision m1). Swahili has no title for this office, so it names him by those he commanded, with the supplied words in brackets at Literal. The chief priests are "wakuu wa makuhani" at every level, as across the New Testament drafts.

source.text: παραγενόμενος δέ τις ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οὓς ἔθεσθε ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ εἰσὶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστῶτες καὶ διδάσκοντες τὸν λαόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having arrived then someone reported to them that, Behold the men whom you put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people.

en.L: Then someone came and reported to them, "Look, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."
en.B: Then a man arrived with news for them: "Those men you locked up are in the temple right now, standing there teaching the people!"
en.R: Then someone came and said to them, "Listen! The men you put in jail are in the temple courts. They are standing there, teaching the people!"

es.L: Entonces llegó alguien y les informó: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, los hombres que {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} en la cárcel están en el templo, de pie y enseñando al pueblo».
es.B: Entonces llegó un hombre con esta noticia: «¡Esos hombres que {{plural_you:encerraron|encerrasteis}} están ahora mismo en el templo, de pie, enseñando al pueblo!».
es.R: Entonces alguien llegó y les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Los hombres que {{plural_you:metieron|metisteis}} en la cárcel están en los patios del templo. ¡Están allí de pie, enseñando a la gente!».

fr.L: Alors quelqu’un arriva et leur rapporta : « Voici, les hommes que vous avez mis en prison sont dans le temple, debout, et enseignent le peuple. »
fr.B: Alors un homme arriva avec cette nouvelle : « Les hommes que vous avez enfermés sont en ce moment dans la cour du temple, debout, en train d’enseigner le peuple ! »
fr.R: Alors quelqu’un est venu leur dire : « Écoutez ! Les hommes que vous avez mis en prison sont dans la cour du temple. Ils sont là, debout, et ils enseignent le peuple ! »

sw.L: Basi mtu mmoja akafika, akawapa habari, "Tazameni, wale watu mliowaweka gerezani wako hekaluni, wamesimama na kuwafundisha watu."
sw.B: Kisha mtu mmoja alifika na habari kwao: "Wale watu mliowafunga gerezani wako hekaluni sasa hivi, wamesimama wakiwafundisha watu!"
sw.R: Kisha mtu mmoja alikuja akawaambia, "Sikilizeni! Watu mliowatia gerezani wako katika nyua za hekalu. Wamesimama pale wakiwafundisha watu!"

decisions.choice: standing: openly, just as the angel told them
decisions.reason: The angel said, "Go and stand in the temple" (5:20); they did exactly that.

decisions.choice: look: a word to draw attention
decisions.reason: The word calls for attention to something surprising.

decisions.choice: right now, with an exclamation
decisions.reason: Balanced conveys the surprise without an archaic "behold".

source.text: τότε ἀπελθὼν ὁ στρατηγὸς σὺν τοῖς ὑπηρέταις ἤγαγεν αὐτούς, οὐ μετὰ βίας, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν, μὴ λιθασθῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone the captain with the officers brought them, not with force, they were fearing for the people lest they be stoned.

en.L: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with force, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.
en.B: The captain then went with his officers and fetched the apostles. They used no violence, for they were afraid of the crowd and of being stoned.
en.R: So the captain and his men went and brought the apostles back. But they did not hurt them or force them to come. They were afraid that the people would throw stones at them.

es.L: Entonces el capitán fue con los alguaciles y los trajo, no con violencia, porque temían al pueblo, no fueran a ser apedreados.
